clue.text: Stools are unable to 'urt?

definitions.meaning: stools have a seat and legs but nothing to rest your elbows on
the dropped-H spelling 'urt for hurt asks for a Cockney rendering of an adjective meaning incapable of injury

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether stools could ever hurt anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'urt signals a dropped H, so the word meaning harmless loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Stools lack the side supports a chair has, so they are without arms; the second sense is harmless said with the H dropped.

clue.text: Praise a second course about mountain climbing

indicators.note: about means the dessert goes round the mountain

parts.note: pud, short for pudding, is the dessert course

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A pudding course praised by a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads the mountain upwards, and 'about' wraps the dessert round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to praise, literally by clapping and more broadly by commending.

clue.text: Continental relative of mine drops second name, which the 9 saw through

indicators.note: drops second means the later of the two name letters is removed

parts.note: mon oncle is French for my uncle

explanation.surface: A European uncle loses his middle name, which a cartoon villain saw through.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is the Batman foe, who wears a single eyeglass; MON ONCLE without its second N gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman's bird-named villain is drawn peering through a single round eyeglass, so this is what he looks through.

clue.text: Develop English leader over old Italian one

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: An English leader develops above an old Italian dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands in for leader, so the old Italian one is the Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or develop something latent, such as an idea.

clue.text: Cooler head under this UN leadership in fix

indicators.note: in places the UN and leadership pieces inside the fix word

parts.note: to set is to fix
taken as written
the helm means command or leadership

explanation.surface: The UN leadership is in a fix about something cooling.
explanation.walkthrough: A sun helmet is a pith hat worn against tropical heat; 'in' puts the leadership inside 'fix'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith hat worn in hot climates keeps the head cool, so a head sits under it to stay cooler.

clue.text: White people on unemployment benefit the state rejected

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
something rejected is sent back, so these two pieces are read in reverse order and backwards

parts.note: UB is the old British abbreviation for unemployment benefit, as in the UB40 card
LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Louisiana
men means people in the general sense

explanation.surface: A complaint that people claiming unemployment benefit were turned away by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the abbreviation and the state together, giving ALBU; 'on' sets the people after.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, the clear part that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: Use as a fruit, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to use something is to put it to work
the adjective formed from the name of a common orchard fruit, meaning like that fruit

explanation.surface: Asking whether something can be put to use as a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply something is to use it, and read as apple-y the word means fruit-like.

clue.text: "Mad world I found in plot", as finished by Sassoon?

indicators.note: found in means the reworked letters are placed inside the plot word

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: mad signals that the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A line of mad poetry in the style of the war poet Siegfried Sassoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Sassoon looks like the war poet; he is Vidal Sassoon, the hairdresser. 'Mad' rearranges the fodder as LOWDRI, and 'found in' puts it in the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair styled at a Vidal Sassoon salon would be finished off with a hand dryer and brush.

clue.text: 11 of FG: 11? Catholic individual put in mix with Nazis

indicators.note: put in places the run of theme, Catholic and individual inside the mixing word

parts.note: to mingle is to mix
the second 11 with its question mark asks what links all the 11 clues, the puzzle's subject
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single individual
SS were the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A Catholic person is thrown in with a group of Nazis.
explanation.walkthrough: FG is Flash Gordon. The query '11?' asks what all the 11 clues share: the puzzle's subject. 'put in' places that, Catholic and individual inside the mixing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruthless emperor of the planet Mongo is the chief foe of Flash Gordon in the comic strips and films.

clue.text: Unpleasant sort of stock admitting one into student union

indicators.note: into puts the stock piece inside the student union letters

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

indicators.note: admitting means the stock cube lets the one inside

parts.note: OXO is a British brand of stock cube
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nasty stock that lets someone into the student union.
explanation.walkthrough: OXO is a well-known British stock cube; 'admitting' and 'into' nest the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noxious is harmful or very unpleasant, often said of fumes.

clue.text: 11 of B, source of literature that's black and white?

definitions.meaning: 11 is the arch-enemy and B is Batman, whose villains include a bird-like criminal in a top hat

definitions.text: source of literature that's black and white?
definitions.meaning: a publishing house of paperbacks named after a black and white flightless bird

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue about a Batman foe and a famous book publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is arch-enemies; letters after 'of' are the initials of the hero, here Batman.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman's foe Oswald Cobblepot goes by the bird's name, and the paperback publisher is named after the same black and white bird.

clue.text: Fabulous bird no charge, so to speak?

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are to be pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a fee (charge) of nix (nothing) is said as fee-nix

explanation.surface: A mythical bird described as costing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fee-nix, a charge of nothing, is said exactly like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical bird that rises from its own ashes is a creature of fable, hence fabulous.

clue.text: Female in church cuts pack to reveal Joker, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece cuts another when it slices into the middle of it

parts.note: an army is a large pack or crowd

indicators.note: in places the female word inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for Church of England
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman in church cuts a deck of cards and turns up the joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' looks like a card in the pack; it is Batman's foe. 'in' and 'cuts' nest the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Joker is Batman's greatest foe, an example of a principal enemy.

clue.text: Female in church cuts pack to reveal Joker, perhaps: some find it tough

definitions.text: Female in church cuts pack to reveal Joker, perhaps

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: The previous clue repeated, with a remark that solvers find it hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue above repeated word for word, so the repeat itself means the same again; the letters sit inside find it tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning the same as before; repeating the previous clue verbatim is exactly what that word stands for.

clue.text: Shift bandage

definitions.meaning: a shift is a simple loose frock
to bandage a wound is to put a covering on it

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a type of frock, and to bandage is to cover a wound with a fresh lint, so both senses fit the word.

clue.text: Flower, source of drug, perhaps?

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A flower described as the origin of some narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of drug' reads as WELL of SPEED, written SPEED then WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell, or veronica, is a small plant with blue blooms.

clue.text: See 7
Regret holding everyone up — it's offensive

indicators.note: holding means the regret word contains the other piece

parts.note: to repent is to regret

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A remorseful person holding everyone up, which is objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses everyone to LLA, and 'holding' puts it inside the regret word.
explanation.definitionFit: A repellant thing is one that disgusts or offends, so the phrase describes it as offensive.

clue.text: Fool put on stage demonstrating rigid movement

parts.note: a goose is a silly person
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A clown on stage shows off a stiff way of moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' just joins the pieces in order; 'demonstrating' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff-legged military march, legs kept straight, is a famously rigid way of moving.

clue.text: Mercenary: good one causing friction?

parts.note: a rubber rubs things, creating friction

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune, good at stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubber is someone greedy for money, as in money-grubber, hence a mercenary type.

clue.text: Black throne room in dark blue city not in favour of reddish-brown

indicators.note: in places the black and throne room pieces inside the shortened city
not means the following phrase is taken away

parts.note: Oxford University's colour is dark blue, as opposed to Cambridge's light blue
for means in favour of
B is black, as on pencils
loo is slang for the toilet, jokingly the throne room

explanation.surface: A gloomy royal chamber in Oxford that dislikes a reddish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the favour word from the city, leaving OXD; 'in' places the rest inside. Oxford's university colour is dark blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxblood is a deep reddish-brown colour, named after the blood of cattle.

clue.text: 11 of LS's race had to claim victory over ruler

indicators.note: over here means placed before the ruler

parts.note: to dart is to race

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the had piece goes round the victory letter

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword ruler

explanation.surface: A runner in a race claims victory over a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: LS is Luke Skywalker of Star Wars. HAD wraps V to make HVAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-masked Sith Lord is the principal foe of Luke Skywalker, and turns out to be his father.

clue.text: Carnival scene can start to generate public disorder

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A carnival can kick off public unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioting is violent public disturbance by a crowd.

clue.text: Celebrity's stolen picture

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a shot is a photograph

explanation.surface: A star's photo has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is an important or highly successful person, a big name.

clue.text: Spontaneous note well hidden in pound, unopened

indicators.note: hidden in puts the note well abbreviation inside the money word
unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a quid is slang for a pound sterling
NB is nota bene, Latin for note well

explanation.surface: A spontaneous note tucked away inside a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the first letter of the money, leaving UID, and 'hidden in' tucks the note inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbidden comes without being asked, which is to say spontaneously or of its own accord.

clue.text: 11 of HP's protest, having run into something potentially shocking

indicators.note: into puts the protest and run inside the shocking word

parts.note: a volt is a unit of electrical potential, so it can deliver a shock
a demo is a protest march
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A protest runs into something that might give people a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is Harry Potter; 'into' puts the protest and run inside the shocking unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark wizard who killed the boy's parents is Harry Potter's chief foe throughout the novels.

clue.text: See 19
Encourage gastronome to swallow his own head?

indicators.note: to swallow means the gastronome's name takes in another letter

parts.note: Egon Ronay was a famous food critic whose guides rated British restaurants
the head of the word gastronome itself, its first letter

explanation.surface: Urging a food lover to eat his own head.
explanation.walkthrough: The gastronome is Egon Ronay; EGON swallows G, the head of the word gastronome.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them, often to do something rash.

clue.text: 11 of JB's b-brain without a drug left, died

indicators.note: without means the named letter is removed

parts.note: the stammered b- gives B before loaf, slang for brain as in use your loaf
E is ecstasy
L is left

explanation.surface: James Bond's foe is stammering about losing his mind after a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: JB is James Bond. The stutter b-brain gives B plus LOAF; take out A to get BLOF.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-stroking head of SPECTRE is James Bond's recurring principal foe in the books and films.

clue.text: An outburst about one's misery

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the outburst goes round the one

parts.note: a gush is a sudden outburst
I is one; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: An emotional outburst over someone's unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the outburst wraps round the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental suffering, a synonym for deep distress.

clue.text: 11 of B, one peppering with shot?

definitions.meaning: 11 is the arch-enemy and B is Batman, whose foes include a puzzle-setting criminal in green
someone who fills a target full of holes with gunfire

explanation.surface: A Batman villain who sprays people with gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to pierce with many holes, so one who does so with shot fits, and Edward Nygma is a Batman foe.

clue.text: Time for this PM to close report, ultimately

parts.note: taken as written
nigh means close or near

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister has until the end of the day to wrap up a report.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister; it is post meridiem, the afternoon and evening.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the time later today after noon, which is what this PM means.
